sections.name: File setup, recencyOf
sections.title: Imports and recency rule
sections.what: Brings in shared helpers and defines recency: a signal's newest source publish date, or the day the monitor first saw it when no source date exists.
sections.why: Likely reason: lists are sorted by what is newest in the evidence, with first-seen as a fallback.
sections.watch_out: A signal with no source dates sorts by when the monitor first saw it, so older material first seen recently can rise to the top.

sections.name: dateLabel, regionsOf, regionName, RowProps
sections.title: Date text, region helpers and row settings
sections.what: Writes the date line on each signal (the newest publish date, or a first-seen date if none), lists the regions a signal belongs to, gives the unmapped group a readable name, and defines the settings each row needs.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are small helpers that keep each row's date and region text consistent.
sections.watch_out: A signal can belong to several regions, so it will show up in more than one regional tab.

sections.name: Row
sections.title: One signal row
sections.what: Draws one signal with its title, tier, countries, type, stage, solution, capex, date and Yard status. When linked, the status links to the matching Yard project, and clicking the row opens the signal.
sections.why: Likely reason: every regional list uses the same row, so mapping and Yard status are visible together.
sections.watch_out: A missing Yard status is shown as pending, so a signal with no status can look like a sync is still in progress.

sections.name: List
sections.title: List container
sections.what: Puts a titled list with a count and a short note above the rows, or shows an empty message when there are no rows.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It is reused for the regional and cross-region lists.
sections.watch_out: The count in the header is for the list shown, so a filter that changes the list changes the count too.

sections.name: RegionalViews
sections.title: Regional views with tabs
sections.what: Shows a cross-region tab first, with recently announced new projects and problem signals. Each region has its own tab listing all its signals with a country breakdown. Also shows Yard status counts, a sync button, and a note on when Yard sync adds a project.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets users switch between one region's full picture and a summary across all regions.
sections.watch_out: Totals across regional tabs can exceed the number of signals, because a signal in two regions is counted in both.

summary: Shows opportunity signals grouped by region, plus a cross-region summary of newly announced projects and problem signals, along with each signal's Yard link status.
purpose: Lets a team see the opportunities in each region and which ones have been linked to, added to, or held back from the Yard project record.
why: Likely reason: regional teams need their own view, and the cross-region view surfaces the most time-sensitive items.
how: Groups signals by region, sorts each group by the newest source date (falling back to when the monitor first saw the signal), counts Yard link states, and shows a row for each signal. A button starts a Yard sync.
inputs: Lists of signals, solutions and the codebook, a callback to open a signal, a callback to start a Yard sync, and a flag that shows the sync is running.
outputs: Tabs for each region and the cross-region view, Yard status counts, signal rows with links, and a sync button.
risks: A signal in more than one region appears in each region, so totals across tabs can exceed the total signal count. Yard sync only adds a project when the evidence quotes its name, industry, stage and country.
debug: If a region tab is empty, check the region mapping of the signal's locations. If dates look wrong, check the publish dates and the first-seen date. If Yard status looks stuck at pending, check whether a sync has run. The count line for a country may need a look if a location lacks a country name.
